segments.text: - When facilitating usability testing,
introducing the participant to the session
is extremely important.
It can help to reassure participants,
make them feel comfortable,
and set their expectations for the session.
- We'll show you how we typically welcome test participants.
I'll play the facilitator for this demo.
- And I'll be the participant.
- So, if you'd like to take a seat over here
and I'll sit here.
- Okay.
- So Kate, thanks for coming in today.
So before we get started,
I just want to give you a little bit of information
about the session and what to expect.
So as you know, the session will last for 60 minutes.
Your participation is voluntary,
so if you do want to take a break
or stop the session, that's absolutely fine.
Feel free to let me know.
Also, if you have questions
about how the session will proceed,
feel free to ask me at any point.
Part of this study, Kate,
is to look at the design of this particular website
that you're going to be using,
and I'm gonna be asking you to do some activities
on this website and to give your feedback.
So, we're really doing this to learn
how we can make this design easier for people to use.
- Okay.
- As you're working on your activities,
it'd be really helpful if you could try and think out loud.
So let me know what you're thinking
as you're sort of moving through the site.
If you're reading anything,
perhaps read a little bit of it out loud.
If you're clicking on a link,
maybe tell me what you're expecting to find there.
- Okay.
- And feel free to be open and honest
with anything that comes to mind.
You know, your feedback is going to be really helpful
for us to improve this particular design.
So I'll be giving you quite a few different activities
to do on the website today.
Some of these are gonna be short,
and others are going to be longer.
Please just work at your own pace,
so do whatever you would do normally.
Please imagine, you know, I'm not here
and you're at home trying these activities
in your own spare free time.
- Okay.
- When you complete an activity or
if you would like to stop, please just let me know.
You can say I'm done or I'd like to stop here,
and that'll be really helpful for me
to know to move you on to the next activity.
Just to let you know,
we're not testing you in any shape or form.
- Okay. - We're testing the design.
So please feel free to be open and honest
about what you think about it.
If there's something that you're struggling with,
please feel free to share that with us.
That's helpful information for us to learn
so that we can improve that experience for other people.
- Yeah. Alright.
- So Kate, just to let you know, I'll be taking notes
as you work on your activities, and I'll probably be quiet
for most of the time.
I may jump in and ask a question,
and I might also direct you to a different area
of the website or move you onto another activity.
That's just part of the process.
So I just want you to make you aware of that.
As you probably noticed in the consent form
that you filled out, we're planning to record the session,
so we'd love to record, you know, what we're talking about.
Also the screen and also through the webcam here as well.
Would that be okay with you?
- Yeah, that's fine.
- Okay, great. Thank you.
It's a good idea to keep an intro script
with you during the session.
That way you'll make sure to communicate
all these important points to your participant.
- After you've run lots of sessions,
you'll probably find that you need
to rely on your script less and less.
Eventually, you might be comfortable
with a simple bulleted list of points
instead of a full script.
